Jai —

Appreciate the clear list. I've attached our SIG answers PDF and a simple diagram of retention boundaries. High-level answers below; Rishi will add a short note about training practices.

1) Prompt/log persistence: For our hosted API, prompt and completion logs (raw request/response payloads) are retained for 30 days by default to support debugging, abuse detection, and billing investigations. Access is limited to a small set of SRE and Security staff via RBAC and audited through our central logging system.

2) Model training on customer data: By default, Redwood does not use individual customer prompt/response logs to perform model training or to fine-tune hosted models. Customers can opt in to a "data contribution" program if they explicitly allow their data to be used to improve models; this is a contract-level option and requires documented consent and a separate data share mechanism.

3) Variation by deployment:
- Hosted API: default prompt logs retained 30 days; metadata aggregates (usage metrics) retained 13 months for billing/analytics.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): customers control retention and can request shorter/longer windows; default if not configured is 30 days.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): retention is under customer control; Redwood does not retain customer data in our control plane beyond metadata for billing unless agreed in contract.

Attachments: SIG_healthcare_answers_20261004.pdf (answers and evidence), retention_diagram_20261004.png (diagram).

I'll defer to Rishi on the training wording to make sure we don't overcommit.

Jai —

Quick answers from security/ops: 

- Exports: Raw prompt log exports require a formal request. For hosted customers, we only produce exports to the customer or their authorized delegate. The request route is via the Console (export request), which raises a ticket to SRE. Exports require (1) authenticated account owner approval or signed POA, (2) justification, and (3) a ticket tracked in our incident system (audit trail retained 3 years). Operationally, exports are staged in an encrypted bucket for 24 hours and are accessible only to the customer and the SRE staff performing the export.

- Downstream analytics: We derive aggregated metrics (latency, token counts, error rates) from logs; aggregated metrics do not contain raw prompt or completion text. Feature stores do not receive raw prompt text as part of standard pipelines. Any pipeline that would use textual data for analytics or product telemetry is limited to tokenized or hashed artifacts and requires a documented Non-Prod/Data Science exception approval.

- 30-day enforcement: For hosted logs the default retention is 30 days and enforced by automated lifecycle policies in our storage layer. Support cannot "restore" deleted raw logs after lifecycle deletion. We can, however, provide aggregated metrics or retained admin audit logs that persist longer (see attachment). For Dedicated customers we will honor requests to set custom retention in the contract; for Private deployments the customer controls retention.

If you want, we can provide a one-page export procedure (SOP) and the excerpt of our RBAC policy for your vendor file — happy to share through the secure link.
